contract: Reusable scalar comparison state admits its modeled 512-byte object/seven-property metadata before construction. Metadata remains charged while the workspace exists, including consumer failures and reuse, and releases on disposal or after an active comparison observes closed scope/reader state. Owned top-k creates the workspace only for allocation-producing scalar shapes when candidate capacity is nonzero. Allocation-free shapes retain their prior budget boundary.

validation.negativeControl: Setting only metadata admission to zero causes both new boundary/integration tests to fail because expected budget rejection does not occur. Restoring the implementation passes all 30 workspace/top-k tests.
cases: Exact metadata capacity and one byte below
Reclamation closing the scope during workspace creation
Input owner retained after workspace admission failure
Consumer failure and subsequent reuse retain metadata but release scalar payloads
Active decoder/comparator disposal and parent-stage disposal retain metadata and payload through settlement
Existing same-entry reuse, union leaves, fixed-stage growth and allocation-free physical execution boundaries

release.checks: build, types, package consumers, compatibility, changeset, deterministic fixtures, large files, lint and unchanged coverage thresholds passed

validation.cloudFixtures: Native R2 four-job owned top-k fixtures at 64/128 MiB pools include ASCII, BMP and supplementary Unicode keys, cache eviction and retained owners. Existing real HTTP fixture coverage passes in the regular suite.

performance.scope: Local real DuckDB-generated Parquet, six cardinality/batch-size cases, every output row checked. Fallback runs move in opposite timing directions; no speedup or cloud-throughput claim. Overall fixture peaks remain unchanged because larger allocations dominate.

remaining: Broader operator/parser/codec ownership and runtime headroom
